corrections.claimed_speedup: docs/ECM_Montgomery_STAGE1.md section 14.2, M4001, stage 1 only, one thread, per curve: B1=1e5 0.596 s vs GMP-ECM 1.787 s (3.00x faster); B1=1e6 6.264 s vs 15.008 s (2.40x); B1=2e6 13.455 s vs about 30 s (GMP-ECM value scaled, about 2.2x). Section 14.5 size sweep at B1=1e6 (README labels these rows measured, only M5755 and M8527 fitted): M1277 0.979 s vs 2.484 s (2.54x), M2203 2.285 s vs 5.804 s (2.54x), M3001 4.137 s vs 9.586 s (2.32x), M3500 5.164 s vs 11.656 s (2.26x), M4001 6.290 s vs 14.624 s (2.32x); about 1.7x at M5755 and M8527 and about 1.75x at M19701 (all columns fitted). Section 10.4 (earlier, before clock pinning), same-machine GMP-ECM ecm-zen3.exe, B2=B1: M1277 B1=1e5 0.135 vs 0.234 s per curve (1.74x), M1277 B1=1e6 1.418 vs 3.551 s (2.50x), M3001 B1=1e5 0.526 vs 1.148 s (2.18x). Against Prime95 v31.04b05 (a model calibrated on one measured M3001 point, 5.65 s, plus the M4001 B1=1e7 run; the 14.2 Prime95 values at B1 1e5-2e6 are scaled from 1e7): 32.7x at M127, 10.4x at M521, 3.94x at M1277, 1.37x at M3001, 0.90x at M4001, 0.17x at M19701 (fitted); the doc recommends the new code below about 3700 bits and Prime95 above about 6000 bits.
corrections.caveats: All GMP-ECM comparisons use Mersenne numbers 2^k-1, where this code switches to a folded-domain reduction that the README says makes 2^k-1 about 2x faster than a general integer of the same size; no comparison on general N is published, and the doc does not show whether GMP-ECM's own special 2^k+-1 arithmetic was active. One author, one laptop-class machine (Ryzen AI 9 HX 370, 256-bit FPU datapath) with hand-pinned clocks, and Prime95 was running on other cores during the section 14 measurements (doc says single-thread numbers reproduce to about +-3%). The section 14.5 footnote says the fit (about 2.98e-7*k^2 + 3.79e-4*k s) built from the measured 1277-4001-bit points extrapolates the larger sizes, and the README table marks only M5755 and M8527 as fitted, so the 1277-4001 rows read as measurements; the M4001 row (6.290/14.624 s) differs slightly from section 14.2 (6.264/15.008 s), suggesting a separate run. The 'about 30 s' GMP-ECM figure at B1=2e6 is scaled, not measured; the section 10.4 numbers predate clock pinning; the doc gives -c 8 in section 14.1 and -c 2 in section 14.4 for GMP-ECM. The prebuilt GMP-ECM binary's compiler and flags are unknown. Stage 1 only (stage 2 is handed to GMP-ECM or Prime95). The repo changes daily (2026-10-02 commits are on the GPU stage 2 path) and the numbers, dated 2026-09-24, were not re-run against HEAD. The scalar GMP mpn backend is only a cross-check (about 5.6 s/curve at M1277, B1=1e5, versus 0.135 s/curve for SIMD), so there is no win against raw GMP mpn arithmetic to claim. GPU backends (CUDA CGBN, OpenCL) are not covered by this entry. GPL-3.0.

notes: Numbers all found on the doc page; the README carries the same section 14.5 table. Main scope limit: the 2.3-3x margin over GMP-ECM is for Mersenne inputs only, where the code uses a special folded reduction. download.mersenne.ca (baseline binary source) was EGRESS_BLOCKED; its existence comes from a WebSearch snippet.

corrections.caveats: Tier capped at C under the project rule for numbers measured on code later fixed for correctness bugs: all files under results/ date from 2026-06-17 (path history: 8a6c6d0, 2abf635, 8619fe3, b8d936e, fd6d149), while 2785394 (2026-08-14, adds Fix.pdf, the corrected proof for floor rather than ceiling rounding reported by Peter Rindal), 145f864 (2026-08-14, 'matrix no k convert to negative'; changes precompute.hpp, cpu/vector/changebase.hpp and cpu/vector/conversion.hpp by a few lines each, plus parameter files) and 0131695 (2026-08-28, constants such as r1_shifted_quotient_estimations 65 to 64 and a floor flag) came later. The diffs look like constant and rounding-mode changes rather than extra hot-path operations, but the benchmarks were not re-run. Same-machine pair, but BLST is built at -O2 -fno-builtin with assembly_small.S (its upstream default) while VROOM uses -O3 -march=native; the pairing figure uses BLST's inverter for the Fp inversion inside the RNS pairing (BM_Pairing_RNS_BLST_Inverter); amortized batch rows exclude any batching cost on the caller side; BLST is a modified vendored copy (extern "C" changes, Apache-2.0 subtree under blst/). The README says timings depend strongly on clang 21; GCC and older clang are 'significantly slower'. Research-grade code, 'not vetted or audited for security' (README). Requires AVX-512 IFMA. The paper (IACR ePrint 2026/393) could not be opened (eprint.iacr.org blocked), so its venue and numbers are unchecked. The task lead's baselines (GMP, MPFR) are not what this repo benchmarks against; BLST is the relevant incumbent for BLS12-381.

notes: All quoted ratios verified row by row on the results page; single-thread confirmed from the raw JSON. Tier stays C only because of the post-measurement correctness fixes; a re-run on HEAD would justify A.
